source.note: The dataset spans multiple VMs/languages (2 of the 31 projects checked incidentally during selection were CosmWasm/Rust or Move, not Solidity — e.g. mantra-dex's own top finding is in a .rs file, so it was excluded below in favor of a confirmed-Solidity project). This catalog picks 10 of the 555 vulnerabilities as a representative, verified-Solidity sample — 1 High/Critical finding each from 10 distinct real projects across all 3 platforms (7 code4rena, 2 sherlock, 1 cantina), not an attempt to catalog the full 555. Each description below is paraphrased directly from the dataset's own finding text (verbatim excerpts read this session, not re-derived from the target repo's actual current source), consistent with source_richness: high for the finding's OWN claim, not an independent re-audit of the code.

cases.title: killGauge() will lead to wrong calculation of emission
cases.description: VoterUpgradeableV2.sol's killGauge() (ve(3,3)-style gauge voting, GOVERNANCE_ROLE-gated) only clears isAlive/claimable and decrements totalWeightsPerEpoch for the CURRENT epoch when disabling a gauge, but distribute() computes emissions using weightsPerEpoch entries that persist for the gauge across OTHER epochs too — so a killed gauge's stale per-epoch weight keeps distorting the emission split among still-active gauges instead of being fully zeroed out.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes exact file/line citations (VoterUpgradeableV2.sol#L239, #L630-L639)

cases.title: Users may encounter losses on assets deposited through StrategySupplyERC4626
cases.description: StrategySupplyERC4626's _deploy()/_undeploy()/_getBalance() return the amount of ERC-4626 SHARES received/burned rather than the underlying ASSET amount, so any BakerFi vault built on this strategy miscalculates the user's real asset position wherever it treats that return value as an asset amount — a straightforward but high-impact unit-confusion bug in a leveraged-vault accounting path.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, with exact file/line citations for all three affected functions

cases.title: Router address validation logic error prevents valid router assignment
cases.description: GenesisPoolManager.setRouter(address _router) is owner-gated but its guard reads `require(_router == address(0), "ZA")` — the exact INVERSE of the zero-address check it clearly intends (reject zero, not require it) — so the only value the function will ever accept is address(0), permanently blocking the owner from ever assigning a real router needed for DEX liquidity operations during a GenesisPool launch.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes the exact one-line buggy require() quoted

cases.title: Buffer silently locks staked HYPE without a withdrawal or L1-transfer path
cases.description: StakingManager's liquidity buffer (meant to serve KHYPE withdrawal queues without touching L1-staked HYPE) can end up holding user HYPE that is never actually used to service queued withdrawals and has no function to pull it back out or move it to L1 for staking — once funds land there via this path they're stuck, permanently idle and unreachable by users or the protocol's own operational flows.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes exact StakingManager.sol line-range citations across three code sections

cases.title: Lack of access control in AgentNftV2::addValidator() enables unauthorized validator injection
cases.description: AgentNftV2::addValidator() has NO access control at all, unlike the ROLE-gated mint(). Because AgentFactoryV2::executeApplication()'s next agent id is predictable via a public nextVirtualId() view, an attacker can front-run agent creation by calling addValidator() first for that not-yet-minted virtualId, injecting themselves as a validator and corrupting the reward-accounting set the legitimate mint() later assumes is empty/trusted.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes exact AgentNftV2.sol line citation

cases.title: execute calls can be front-run
cases.description: MinimalDelegation's execute() (Uniswap's EIP-7702-style delegation contract) is publicly callable by anyone holding a valid signature, since the signed digest never binds the intended executor's identity — so any party who obtains a signed batched call (e.g. one requiring msg.value) can front-run it with msg.value=0, forcing part of the batch to revert, or otherwise consume the signature/nonce first and make the legitimate submitter's own subsequent call revert.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read in full (this one has no separate code-diff block, description itself is the complete write-up)

cases.title: Market coordinator can steal all market collateral by changing adiabatic fees
cases.description: Perennial V2's market coordinator role has broad control over market parameters, explicitly bounded by protocol parameters meant to prevent theft even from a malicious coordinator (per the project's own stated threat model). The report found that even while every individual parameter stays within its documented "reasonable" bounds, a coordinator can still drain all market collateral purely by manipulating the ADIABATIC FEE (a fee taken from takers meant to price order-flow imbalance) — the protocol acknowledged this as valid despite parameters technically staying in-bounds.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes the project's own README threat-model quote and the acknowledged status

cases.title: Requested tip is not deducted from the depositor's reward checkpoint
cases.description: GovernanceStaker sends a caller-requested tip to the tip receiver but never subtracts that tip amount from the depositor's own scaledUnclaimedRewardCheckpoint, so the tip is effectively paid OUT OF THE POOL on top of what the depositor is still credited for — draining rewards owed to other legitimate stakers (a rewards-insolvency bug, not merely a rounding issue). Fix quoted directly in the report: subtract `_requestedTip * SCALE_FACTOR` from the checkpoint alongside the existing safeTransfer.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes the exact one-line fix diff quoted from the report

cases.title: A single depositor can grief other depositors via early-epoch withdrawal-request claims
cases.description: IdleCreditVault.claimWithdrawRequest() allows a withdrawal request submitted during the CDO's pre-first-epoch deposit/withdrawal window to be CLAIMED immediately, before the first epoch has even ended — the condition meant to gate claims on epoch completion doesn't actually enforce that boundary, letting a single depositor front-run other depositors' seeded liquidity before the epoch it was meant to fund even starts.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes the annotated (@audit-issue) claimWithdrawRequest() snippet from the report

cases.title: Lack of slippage protection on AMM swaps during liquidity removal
cases.description: Two distinct code paths in VaultLib (redeemEarly's _liquidateLpPartial -> _redeemCtDsAndSellExcessCt, and a related liquidate-unchecked path) call the AMM router's swapExactTokensForTokens with a hardcoded minimum-output of 0 and a deadline of block.timestamp — both slippage protection and deadline enforcement are effectively disabled, exposing every early-redemption/liquidity-removal swap in this depeg-hedging protocol to MEV sandwich extraction.
cases.source_richness: high — full dataset finding text read, includes both affected call sites quoted from the report
